bmt-2020-discrete-tiebreaker-01.title: Prime exponents
bmt-2020-discrete-tiebreaker-01.body:
A minimal $n$ has only the primes $2$ and $3$: $n=2^a3^b$. For $\frac n2=2^{a-1}3^b$ to be a square, $a$ is odd and $b$ even; for $\frac n3=2^a3^{b-1}$ to be a cube, $3\mid a$ and $b\equiv1\pmod3$. The smallest such exponents are $a=3$ ($a$ odd, multiple of $3$) and $b=4$ ($b$ even, $b\equiv1\pmod 3$). So $n=2^3\cdot3^4=648$. Check: $648/2=324=18^2$ and $648/3=216=6^3$.

**Answer: 648**

bmt-2020-discrete-tiebreaker-02.title: Count growth histories
bmt-2020-discrete-tiebreaker-02.body:
There are $3^6=729$ equally likely sequences. With $6$ growths, at least $2$ arms, $2$ legs and $1$ nose forces the (arms, legs, noses) counts to be $(3,2,1)$, $(2,3,1)$ or $(2,2,2)$. The number of sequences: $\frac{6!}{3!2!1!}=60$, $60$, and $\frac{6!}{2!2!2!}=90$, total $210$.

The probability is $\frac{210}{729}=\frac{70}{243}$, so $m+n=313$.

**Answer: 313**

bmt-2020-discrete-tiebreaker-03.title: Complementary counting
bmt-2020-discrete-tiebreaker-03.body:
The numbers are distinct and between $1$ and $21$, so $0<|a_i-a_j|\le20$ and $21\nmid a_i-a_j$. Hence $\gcd(a_i-a_j,21)=7$ exactly when $7\mid a_i-a_j$, i.e. when $a_i\equiv a_j\pmod7$.

We want the probability that some two of the three numbers are congruent modulo $7$. The complement is that all three residues mod $7$ differ: after choosing $a_1$, there are $21-3=18$ choices out of $20$ for $a_2$ in a different residue class, then $21-6=15$ out of $19$ for $a_3$. So the complement has probability $\frac{18}{20}\cdot\frac{15}{19}=\frac{27}{38}$, and the desired probability is $\frac{11}{38}$. Thus $m+n=49$.

**Answer: 49**
